question: How many members of Rajya Sabha are nominated by the President ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The President of India has the authority to nominate **12 members** to the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Parliament.
 
• These nominations are intended to ensure that the Rajya Sabha includes individuals with special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as literature, science, art, and social service.
 
• Article **80 of the Indian Constitution** provides for the nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha by the President.
 
• Such nominations help in bringing expert opinion and knowledge into the legislative process, enriching the debates and discussions in the Rajya Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajya Sabha**

 
 
• The Rajya Sabha, or the Council of States, is the upper house of India's bicameral Parliament, with the Lok Sabha being the lower house.
 
• It currently has a maximum membership of 245, of which 233 are elected by the legislatures of the states and union territories using single transferable votes, and 12 are nominated by the President.
 
• The members serve staggered six-year terms, with a third of the members retiring every two years.
 
• The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Article 80 of the Indian Constitution**
 
 
• Article 80 deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• It specifies that the Rajya Sabha shall consist of not more than 250 members.
 
• Of these, 12 members are nominated by the President for their expertise in specific fields such as literature, science, art, and social service.
 
• The remainder of the members are elected by the states and union territories' legislative assemblies.
 
 
 
• **Nomination Process**
 
 
• The President of India nominates individuals to the Rajya Sabha based on their distinguished contribution to various fields.
 
• This process ensures that the Rajya Sabha benefits from the expertise and knowledge of eminent personalities.
 
• Nominations are made in accordance with the provisions of Article 80 of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Role of Nominated Members**
 
 
• Nominated members play a crucial role in enriching the legislative process by providing insights and perspectives from their respective fields.
 
• They are not bound by party affiliations and can contribute independently to the functioning of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• They participate in debates, discussions, and the overall legislative process, bringing in their expert knowledge and experience.
